correctness.rationale: Five-regular triangle-free diameter-two Clebsch graph has exactly 160 maximal three-vertex geodesics. A complement hits them iff it induces maximum degree at most one. Spectral inequality excludes dissociation sets larger than eight and character orthogonality gives only the ten coordinate half-cube maxima. Every one of 65536 subsets is independently tested in both standalone programs, proving the remaining 16 maximal neighborhood sets and exact polynomial. Half-cube intersections and one-step TAR moves mathematically establish the four-position relocation threshold; BFS reconfirms component sizes and exact pair distances. Both programs executed with all assertions passing.

value.rationale: The question concerns all shortest-path hitting placements and their feasible rearrangements on a canonical strongly regular graph; the general complexity of dissociation and geodesic transversals makes the exact graph-specific result motivated. New irredundant size-11 placements occur separately from the previously known optimal size-8 matching supports, causing a 16-component fragmentation spike at budget 11. The exact four-spare threshold and 8/16 move distances quantify the temporary capacity needed for safe reconfiguration, beyond an already known optimum-support classification. The complete polynomial has mathematical content independent of the known minimum geometry.
